facts.fact: An open marketplace, also called an open ad exchange, is an exchange where digital ad placements are bought and sold as part of an auction run through real-time bidding.
facts.quote: An open marketplace (also known as an open ad exchange) is an exchange where digital ad placements are bought and sold as part of an auction.

facts.fact: A private marketplace (PMP) lets a publisher offer its premium inventory to a selected, limited audience of media buyers, and is a subset of real-time bidding.
facts.quote: PMPs are a subset of real-time bidding, but allow a publisher to offer their premium inventory to a selected, limited audience of media buyers.

facts.fact: Premium ad inventory is ad space a publisher has reserved for select advertisers at a set price.
facts.quote: Premium ad inventory is ad space that a publisher has reserved for select advertisers, at a set price.

facts.fact: The page states there are four most common types of programmatic inventory: open marketplace, private marketplace (PMP), preferred deals, and programmatic guaranteed deals.
facts.quote: The four most common ways are through the open marketplace, private marketplace (PMP), preferred deals, and programmatic guaranteed deals.

facts.fact: According to the vendor, the open marketplace is typically the quickest and most cost-efficient way to buy media.
facts.quote: Another benefit of the open marketplace is that it’s typically the quickest and most cost-efficient way to buy media.

facts.fact: According to the vendor, the private marketplace is more expensive than the open marketplace but gives access to premium, more exclusive inventory.
facts.quote: The private marketplace is more expensive, but will deliver you access to premium, more exclusive inventory.
